method.scope: Official framework, platform, cloud-provider and linter documentation, checked against the current Sarj source catalog. This is a policy review, not a production performance study.

method.decisionRule: Prefer the existing owner; recommend a new detector only when it has a source-semantic boundary, concrete harm and a valid-state exclusion.

passes.topic: Upload transport and Python API identity
passes.finding: File accepts multipart request bytes; UploadFile can accept uploads without a File default. The existing root UploadFile ban misses File and its defining modules.
Browser File is a valid fetch body for a direct upload. Server boundary evidence must come from directives or known framework imports; the word File or a filename alone is insufficient.

Issue authorized, limited-lived object capabilities; validate the completed object before trusting it. Provider resumable-session URLs are also direct-upload capabilities and should not be banned for lacking a signed query string.
Use Ruff banned-api and the existing library-policy adapters for exact APIs and packages. Retain the runtime-load companion because ESLint no-restricted-imports only covers static imports.

Python blocking async APIs and Node synchronous filesystem calls already have owners. Imported synchronous child-process, expensive crypto and compression calls in request handlers remain promising context-specific candidates.
Reuse scoped clients. HTTPX already has timeouts by default, and Ruff S113 detects explicitly disabled HTTPX request timeouts; do not invent a missing-timeout ban for all HTTPX calls.
Bound work admission for dynamically sized fanout and respect stream backpressure. TaskGroup and Promise.all remain valid APIs; scheduling supervision is different from a concurrency limit.
Prefer declared bulk operations, explicit projections and cursor pagination where applicable. Sarj already owns bulk, SELECT-star and OFFSET findings; ORM access alone cannot establish an N+1 defect.
Durable workflows need explicit queue/retry contracts. BackgroundTasks, create_task, cache and retry libraries have valid uses and should not receive unconditional bans.

Test aliases, local File classes, type-only imports, client directives, inline server actions, suppression, malformed input and duplicate ownership. Preserve ordinary forms and object-storage SDKs. Publish no runtime speedup claim without application measurements.

findings.harm: Multipart bytes occupy application workers and can be fully buffered when declared as bytes.
findings.validBoundary: Unrelated File symbols, Body/Form metadata, downloads and explained local exceptions remain valid.
findings.fix: Return an authorized upload capability; accept an object key and metadata.

findings.gap: Already banned at the public root.
findings.validBoundary: The pre-existing downloaded-file constructor case from fastapi.datastructures remains allowed; a blanket ban on every UploadFile implementation path would also reject local adapters. Route-aware annotation detection is a separate future gap.

apis: native File references within explicit server boundaries
findings.harm: Makes file ingress and server File adaptation visible to policy.
findings.validBoundary: Browser File, unrelated imports/local classes, Blob, FormData and unknown environments remain allowed.
findings.limitations: Unknown wrappers, re-exports, unmarked Fetch handlers, raw streams and base64 payloads can bypass this syntactic policy. A clean lint result is not proof of a valid storage signature.

findings.owner: LIB120 via existing dependency, static-import and runtime-load adapters
findings.harm: Dedicated server multipart-upload dependencies enable the prohibited transport.
findings.validBoundary: FormData, outbound form-data and @aws-sdk/lib-storage are not banned. A package used solely for string fields still falls under the explicitly requested architectural dependency policy; use ordinary form parsing or a reasoned local exception.

findings.reason: String forms, browser previews, signed POST policies and generated downloads use these APIs legitimately.
findings.nextStep: A future inbound-file dataflow rule must prove request provenance and a File or binary sink.

apis: blocking HTTP/filesystem/process calls in async def
findings.owner: Ruff ASYNC rules selected by the shipped ALL policy
findings.nextStep: Repair a demonstrated upstream gap rather than duplicate its detector.

findings.validBoundary: Startup-only programs, synchronous plugin contracts and explicit durability calls need review.
findings.nextStep: Use corpus evidence before promotion; avoid n/no-sync because unrelated methods ending in Sync are valid.

findings.harm: Long synchronous work blocks other requests on the same event loop.
findings.detectorBoundary: Resolve known builtin imports and prove execution inside a request handler; distinguish true Node APIs from local lookalikes.
findings.validBoundary: CLI tooling, startup-only work, workers and synchronous framework contracts.
findings.nextStep: Create labeled request-handler and CLI corpora; start as warning after a reproduced defect.

findings.limitations: A fetch signal is a cancellation path, not necessarily a deadline. Deliberate streaming and externally managed deadlines need exceptions.
findings.nextStep: Probe the pinned Ruff version before proposing a client-constructor timeout=None extension.

apis: httpx.AsyncClient construction inside a request loop
repeated top-level httpx requests in a hot loop
findings.harm: Recreating clients defeats connection reuse and adds repeated connection setup.
findings.existingOwner: no-async-client-in-constructor covers a different lifecycle defect.
findings.detectorBoundary: Resolve the HTTPX constructor, loop and ownership/close relationship.
findings.validBoundary: One-shot scripts, deliberate per-identity isolation and clients injected from a lifespan scope.
findings.nextStep: Add a warning candidate with loop and lifespan counterexamples.

apis: asyncio.gather over dynamically sized remote work
findings.harm: Unbounded admission can exhaust sockets, pools and memory.
findings.detectorBoundary: Prove the native aggregate and remote work plus the absence of a declared bound; a map method name does not prove array semantics.
findings.validBoundary: Small fixed tuples, bounded worker pools, externally limited iterables and non-I/O tasks.
findings.nextStep: Prototype a warning only after a concrete unbounded workload and limiter near misses are labeled.

apis: read() without size on remote streams
arrayBuffer/blob/text materialization of unbounded inbound bodies
findings.harm: Materializing unbounded data scales memory with payload size.
findings.detectorBoundary: Require remote-stream provenance and a missing validated size/admission bound.
findings.validBoundary: Small checked payloads, browser previews, fixture data and bounded object metadata.
findings.nextStep: Research type/dataflow coverage; avoid a universal ban on read or arrayBuffer.

apis: repeated singleton reads/writes with a declared equivalent bulk method
findings.validBoundary: Order-dependent transactions, incompatible bulk semantics and small independent operations.
findings.nextStep: Reuse the existing declared contracts; measure query counts for opaque ORM cases.

findings.validBoundary: The owning rules document supported query shapes and exceptions.

apis: detached asyncio.create_task for required business work
findings.harm: Required work should not depend on the lifetime of one request worker.
findings.detectorBoundary: Requires an explicit durable-work contract or known business boundary; names such as payment/send do not prove it.
findings.validBoundary: Best-effort cleanup, supervised ephemeral tasks and noncritical notifications.
findings.nextStep: Design an opt-in durability contract and warning; do not ban BackgroundTasks or create_task globally.

findings.harm: Retries can amplify load and repeat side effects during failure.
findings.existingOwner: require-injectable-retry-sleep checks testability, not distributed retry safety.
findings.detectorBoundary: Known retry configuration plus explicit attempt/deadline and idempotency contracts.
findings.validBoundary: Durable consumers with external budgets and explicit idempotency keys.
findings.nextStep: Start with demonstrably infinite known-library configurations; avoid banning all retries or fixed local polling.
Do not duplicate it or ban ordinary synchronous caches.

findings.harm: Unbounded cardinality can retain request-specific data indefinitely.
findings.validBoundary: Finite configuration domains and intentional process-lifetime memoization.
findings.nextStep: Observe memory and key cardinality before designing a warning.
